newsitem.title: NORWAY: Cargo insurance rates under pressure - industry.
newsitem.headline: Cargo insurance rates under pressure - industry.

text.p: Cargo insurance rates are under downward pressure because of increased competition and an abundance of reinsurance capacity, industry sources said at an international conference.

Marine insurance associations from around the world have spelled out their concerns in submissions to their ruling body, the International Union of Marine Insurers (IUMI), which is meeting in Oslo this week.

Member countries have cited increased competition at domestic and international level which, coupled with the relatively good recent claims experience in the market, has allowed brokers to demand substantial discounts from underwriters.
Some countries have reported reductions of more than 30 percent.

Countries such as Greece added that rates are also being pushed down because insurance buyers are making greater use of self insurance, where they accept a high deductible for lower premium and bear the rest of the risk themselves.
Emanuel Burckhardt, chairman of IUMI's cargo committee, told delegates on Monday: "Most markets have reported downward pressure on rates, erosion of profits and a softening market."

"The London market has reported overall stability despite the increase in competition, mainly due to a drop in new business. Increased use of deductibles, especially by large multinational clients, is resulting in the reduction of rates," said Burckardt.
